claims.scope: NVIC and SysTick bounded source contracts only. Exact IRQ declarations remain in hash-bound device inventory; no full Arm architecture, MPU/FPU/CoreSight, fault recovery, RTOS or runtime qualification.
claims.inventory_provenance: Reuse the exact 73 external IRQ declarations, 89 startup external positions and 16 holes in the bound inventory. Family 99-position RM table is not exact-device availability.

contracts.detail: Select only exact named external IRQs from bound inventory, not every integer up to 88. Shared vector ownership and source acknowledgement remain peripheral-specific. Core exceptions have distinct permitted operations; negative IRQ values are not generally valid for external enable/pending APIs.

Priority grouping partitions the same four implemented priority bits globally. Changing grouping changes preemption interpretation of existing priorities without rewriting those bytes. Serialize grouping with all users; RTOS/interrupt-masking constraints and actual delivery latency remain unqualified. Equal programmed priorities use lower IRQ number first per RM.

CMSIS DisableIRQ writes ICER then DSB/ISB, but does not clear NVIC pending, acknowledge peripheral status or await an already-active handler. Separate pending/active getters exist. Inference: disabling alone is not callback/buffer release; stop source, establish ISR completion and lifetime ownership before reuse.

NVIC pending operations change NVIC state only; wrappers do not clear EXTI/peripheral flags. A persistent source can require separate acknowledgement. Software-pending is not proof of physical peripheral operation or timing.

CMSIS SetVector writes vectors[IRQn+16] at current VTOR and issues DSB; its comment requires relocated writable SRAM. It does not validate memory extent, vector target, ownership or concurrent execution. No vector relocation/mutation authorized by this candidate.

SetFreq computes integer ticks=f_source/requested_hz, writes LOAD=ticks-1, clears VAL, enables counter and interrupt. Nominal rate is f_source/ticks, subject to supported timer operation; integer truncation means it need not equal request. Source getter computes from RCC settings/constants, not measurement or readiness. Counter restart changes phase.

RCC permits external HCLK/8, LSI or LSE; LSI/LSE selection requires HCLK period no more than one quarter of source period. RCC source 3 disables kernel clock. Source switch and frequency changes require coordinated reload/timebase updates; no automatic elapsed-time continuity is established. The SDK external clock getter returns 0 for source 3, or for LSE if LSE_VALUE is not defined. For a nonzero requested frequency, SetFreq then computes ticks = 0 and returns HAL_ERROR through SetReload; this zero source value is not a divide-by-zero denominator.

HAL Suspend/Resume only clear/set TICKINT, leaving counter enable and reload unchanged. They do not clear pending SysTick or define elapsed tick accounting. Tick-dependent HAL waits can stop progressing while ISR delivery is masked; this is an integration gate, not a measured hang.

source_derived_SDK_gates.detail: Exact COMP2 branch IS_IRQ_NUMBER checks only irqn <= 88. It admits external holes and every negative value. CMSIS external Enable/Disable ignore negatives, but priority access uses SHPR[((uint32_t)IRQn & 15) - 4]. Reset (-15), NMI (-14) and HardFault (-13) produce unsigned-underflow indices. Reserved -9 through -6 and -3 select reserved slots 3 through 6 and 9; values below -16 alias modulo 16 (for example -17 selects slot 11, SysTick). Admit only the seven explicitly listed settable exceptions or exact named external IRQs. SCB layout places SHPR at offset 0x018 after CCR at 0x014, but out-of-bounds C access does not establish a particular emitted machine address or hardware effect. No observed execution or CCR corruption is claimed. More generally any negative IRQn with low nibble0..3 underflows, including -16 and aliases such as -29; a modulo16 alias is not necessarily a valid SHPR index.

SetPriority/GetPriority read global grouping while separately accessing priority bytes. No lock prevents grouping changes between guard checks/encode/decode. CMSIS Encode masks excessive priority bits; it does not reject them. Debug checks are not runtime range or global ownership validation.

SetFreq rejects zero only through optional runtime checking or debug assertion; with both disabled it divides by zero. Nonzero values producing ticks = 0 or ticks > 0x1000000 fail SetReload before VAL/enable changes. An invalid request does not imply the prior timer was stopped.

SetClkSource changes CLKSOURCE without recalculating LOAD or preserving a specified timebase. SetFreq unconditionally enables TICKINT and counter after programming, potentially overriding a suspended interrupt policy. Neither configures priority or clears pending exception state.
HAL GetPriority checks output pointers only with debug assertions and then dereferences both; caller must validate storage. No optional runtime pointer guard exists in that function.

With debug assertions disabled, CMSIS masks grouping to 0 through 7. With four priority bits, raw PRIGROUP 0 through 2 encode the same four preemption bits and zero subpriority bits as raw 3 (HAL group 4). HAL GetPriorityGrouping returns the raw value cast to its enum, so raw 0 through 2 are not declared HAL enum members. Validate the HAL domain separately; this is source behavior, not an observed configuration.

conflicts.detail: RM440 says 98 external channels while family table numbers 0..98; exact inventory has 73 named external IRQs and gaps. Preserve disagreement and exact declarations, no invented additional channels.
RM440 describes only HCLK/8 as external source, whereas RCC254/316 and SDK getter also support LSI/LSE. Apply source-specific rate and ratio gates instead of assuming HCLK/8 universally.

Family helper comment allows ticks 1 through 0xFFFFFF; its 24-bit LOAD check accepts ticks = 0x1000000 too, giving LOAD = 0xFFFFFF. This is a source-derived helper boundary, not independent proof of useful operation for LOAD = 0 / ticks = 1.
